resolutions.rationale: Minor and correct: 2.1's Verified block compares `HEAD~1` with `HEAD`, which is only the right pair after 2.2's commit; run before it, both refs hold the unformatted files and the loop prints a false `whitespace-only`. No decision is involved. Rather than add an ordering sentence, the cleaner recorded wording makes the oracle order-independent: in 2.1 compare the committed file with the working tree — `[ "$(git show HEAD:$f | tr -d ' \t\n,')" = "$(tr -d ' \t\n,' < "$f")" ]` — run immediately after `biome check --write .` and before the commit; then 2.2's `git show --stat --oneline HEAD` carries the seven-path check alone. This is the same comparison measured in round 2 (WHITESPACE-ORACLE) with the post-commit blob replaced by the working-tree file; I did not re-run it, the substitution is `cat` for `git show HEAD:`. Either this or the readiness lens's one-sentence ordering note closes it; Bambadjan applies one in the tidy pass.
